title: As the ideal German immigrant, I saw how the supremacist integration system enables the far right
sub: The country is dependent on the labour force of young migrants but makes no effort to address racism and create an inclusive society for them.

title: Speculative Money Has Been Turning Millions of People into Commodities
sub: On microfinance, securitisation and household debt in Modi-era India

title: Debt in everyday life: A critique on the increasing role of finance in social policy
sub: One gap that is rarely discussed in research is the increasing penetration of finance within social policy that is further pushing individuals and households into a debt-poverty trap.
source: 2021, originally published by German Development Institute (DIE)

title: 80 Years of Bleeding Us Dry! The Bretton Woods Institutions, Austerity, and Social Protection
sub: On how the World Bank and IMF's austerity conditionality has blocked rights-based social protection systems in the Global South — and what it would take to build one.
source: 2024, Chapter 8, Towards a People’s History of the IMF & World Bank — IBON International

title: From Peripheral Populations to Financial Fiefdoms: A Case Study from Southern India
sub: India is undergoing a crisis of over-indebtedness. Peripheral populations increasingly rely on loans to meet their basic survival needs.

title: Does women’s economic empowerment promote human development in low- and middle-income countries? A meta-analysis
sub: Reducing gender inequality in economic opportunities is considered valuable in its own right and a critical element in ending poverty and boosting economic prosperity.

title: Does economic growth reduce multidimensional poverty? Evidence from low- and middle-income countries
sub: The long-standing tradition of empirical studies investigating the nexus between economic growth and poverty concentrates mainly on monetary poverty.

title: Poverty, Inequality and Growth: the East Asian experience
sub: This chapter focuses on the poverty, inequality and growth trends in four low and middle-income countries in East and South East Asia.
source: 2022, Book Chapter In A. Breuer, D. Malerba, S. Srigiri, & P. Balasubramanian (Eds.), Governing the interlinkages between the SDGs: Approaches, opportunities and challenges

title: Subjective Returns to Education: Rational Expectations of Disadvantaged Groups in India
sub: This study uses data collected from school students in Mumbai to investigate how they perceive subjective expected returns for different levels of education.

title: Arboreal Archives
sub: A 120 year old Oak tree deliberates on questions about solidarity, activism and how to build movements as it witnesses an ongoing one-month protest camp at Oranienplatz in Berlin.

title: Who cares for caregivers
sub: Meenaksi is a health care worker in southern India who discusses the state’s indifference to her work and the burden of increasing digitisation on the last-mile caregiver.

title: Debt Tales
sub: A two day workshop and exhibition that brought together visual artists from marginalised groups to challenge the hegemonic financial system through their art work.
source: 2024, with Anthoni Guruz — workshop and exhibition
